headline: Failed Senate bill would have paid federal workers who must keep working during a government shutdown, instead of making them wait.
what_it_does: The bill would have provided money so federal agencies could pay "excepted employees" on time during a government shutdown. These are workers who are required to keep working when funding lapses. Under current law, they are not paid until the shutdown ends. The bill would have covered regular pay, allowances, benefits, and other payments, and would have applied back to September 30, 2025.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees required to work during a shutdown
who_it_affects.how: They would have received their regular pay and benefits during a shutdown instead of waiting until it ended.

who_it_affects.group: Active-duty members of the Armed Forces
who_it_affects.how: They would have been counted as excepted employees and paid during a shutdown.
Contractors who support federal employees during a shutdown would have been included as excepted employees eligible for payment.
They would have been able to use this money to pay excepted workers only while no regular or temporary funding law was in effect.
